html:
Lamu is a town on an island off the north coast of Kenya, the oldest and best preserved Swahili town still lived in, listed by UNESCO in 2001.

Its narrow streets of coral stone houses with carved wooden doors, mosques and courtyards have changed little for centuries. Donkeys still serve as transport, and dhows sail from its harbour. It traded mangrove poles, ivory and grain across the Indian Ocean.

Lamu came under Omani rule in the 19th century and later British Kenya. It is a centre of Swahili Islamic learning, with the Maulidi festival drawing pilgrims, and of Swahili poetry in the tradition of the Utendi wa Tambuka. It stands among the Swahili city-states of the coast.
sum: Lamu is a town on an island off the north coast of Kenya, the oldest and best preserved Swahili town still lived in, listed by UNESCO in 2001.
